Hero Retirement.text: Pro heroes retire for the same reasons athletes do, and often for harder ones. Many leave when age slows them, since the job demands speed and stamina, and a body that once handled a Quirk easily can start to struggle with it. Injury ends many careers early: a single wound that makes fighting or a Quirk unsafe can force a hero out after one incident, and the public usually learns of it from a short press release. Others step away after a loss, a scandal or simple exhaustion. Retirement is a legal step: the hero notifies the Hero Public Safety Commission, which retires the license. An agency does not outlive its founder automatically. A senior sidekick may take over and run it under a new name, the staff may merge into another agency, or the office may close; fans, sponsors and the patrol area all have to be earned again by whoever stays. Retired heroes rarely disappear. Many teach at hero academies, train young pros privately, consult for agencies or the police, or appear as commentators on hero programs. The press covers the departure of any famous hero at length, and fans argue for months about who will fill the gap on the chart.
